question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's default-on user memory isolation contract, and what exact upgrade/default behavior must be guaranteed before merge?
rationale: The PR defines a privacy boundary, adds new config defaults/options, and changes QMD and builtin memory state layout; automation cannot safely choose the product and security policy for existing shared-memory deployments.

options.title: Require consistent default-on isolation
options.body: Require the runtime to match the schema/docs, honor or remove each accepted option, define upgrade behavior, and provide real two-user builtin plus QMD proof before merge.

options.title: Make isolation opt-in first
options.body: Preserve existing shared-memory behavior by default and add an explicit opt-in isolation mode with proof and docs before considering default-on behavior later.

options.title: Defer to the canonical design issue
options.body: Pause or close this branch and resolve the broader partition identity, legacy-memory, and migration policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/63550 first.

recommendation.title: Require consistent default-on isolation
recommendation.body: Require the runtime to match the schema/docs, honor or remove each accepted option, define upgrade behavior, and provide real two-user builtin plus QMD proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across memory search, QMD, and config-adjacent code and is the best available routing owner for the security/default policy choice.
